name: Tomb of Khai Dinh
kicker: Compact ornate tomb on a renamed hill
summary: The most compact of the royal tombs, about 117 m by 48.5 m on the slope of Ứng Sơn, begun in 1920 and eleven years in the building. Climb the dragon stairs to the carved grey facade, then step inside to the gilded statue of the king. Pair it with Minh Mang or Tu Duc on the four-site ticket.
getThere: Upstream with the other royal tombs, by bicycle or taxi.
heroCaption: The dragon stairs and carved facade of Khai Dinh’s tomb

notice.title: On the four-site ticket
notice.body: Khai Dinh is on the 530,000 VND four-site adult ticket with the Imperial City, Minh Mang, and Tu Duc, valid two days from the first visit. Bought alone, it is 150,000 VND.

body: The centre places the tomb on the slope of Châu Chữ, also called Châu Ê, which the king renamed Ứng Sơn. The plan is about 117 m by 48.5 m. Work started on 4 September 1920 and took 11 years. The centre contrasts that footprint with the larger garden tombs.

An adult ticket is 150,000 VND, and a child from 7 to 12 pays 30,000 VND. Under 7 is free. It sits on the four-site ticket with the Imperial City, Minh Mang, and Tu Duc: 530,000 VND for an adult and 100,000 VND for a child from 7 to 12, for up to two days from the first visit.
Pair it with Minh Mang or Tu Duc rather than giving it a day of its own, and use it if you hold the four-site ticket. Winter ticket sales stop at 17:00.

figures.caption: The view from the upper terrace across the hills
figures.alt: Ornate stone terrace and a small roof at Khai Dinh’s tomb, with hills and a wide sky behind

gettingThere: The tomb is upstream with the other royal tombs, on the hill the king called Ứng Sơn. Go by bicycle or taxi from the south bank.
hours: 16 Mar–15 Oct: 06:30–18:00, tickets until 17:30. 16 Oct–15 Mar: 07:00–17:30, tickets until 17:00 (conservation centre notice, 12 Mar 2024). Confirm the board on arrival.
closed: No weekly closing day on the centre’s notice.
admissionNote: Adult 150,000 VND. A child from 7 to 12 pays 30,000 VND. Under 7 is free. Hue residents and the other groups named in Resolution 55 pay half. The four-site ticket, Imperial City plus Minh Mang, Tu Duc, and Khai Dinh, is 530,000 VND for an adult and 100,000 VND for a child from 7 to 12, for up to two days from the first visit.
